tasks.title: BVA-07 - P3 Retitle the public claim: UNMEASURABLE must survive aggregation

evidence.ref: acceptance: the write-up claims only that UNMEASURABLE must survive aggregation as a refusal - not dropped from the denominator, not counted as passed, not scored as failed, with no configuration path to defeat it - and cites Scorecard, OHDSI summarizeResults.R, XCCDF result_scoring.c and GE expectation_validation_result.py as the contrast set. Migration cost: none, it is a claim change. Falsified by: the published text still asserting that a fourth verdict is itself uncommon.

BUILD-VS-ADOPT-PROMPT.md's closing claim - 'I do not recall seeing UNMEASURABLE as a first-class feature in any scorecard or data-quality product' - is refuted by six sources read at primary: OpenSSF Scorecard InconclusiveResultScore = -1 (and it FIRES: checks/evaluation/code_review.go calls CreateInconclusiveResult); Soda Core CheckOutcome.NOT_EVALUATED vs EXCLUDED; datacontract-cli ResultEnum with seven members; Dagster EXECUTION_FAILED / SKIPPED with those meanings in source comments; W3C EARL earl:CannotTell and earl:NotTested; XCCDF/NIST IR 7275 ERROR/UNKNOWN/NOT_CHECKED. As drafted the claim is falsifiable in four minutes. What survives is that EVERY one of them discards it at the aggregate: Scorecard drops it from the denominator so 10 of 18 inconclusive can still score 10.0/10; OHDSI computes countPassed = countTotal - countOverallFailed so notApplicable and isError round UP to passed; XCCDF scores ERROR and UNKNOWN as 0.0, identical to fail; GE computes unsuccessful = evaluated - successful with successful = sum(exp.success or False) so a crashed instrument counts as failing; Grafana ships a Set-Normal handler for No-Data; pytest greens skipped and xfailed by default. readiness.py:1176 keeps it in the denominator. The representation problem is solved everywhere; the aggregation problem is solved nowhere.
